items.prompt: If I ___ more free time, I would join a choir.

explanation.en: Second conditional: past simple in the if clause.

optionNotes.en: Correct: if + past simple for an unreal present.
Would never goes in the if clause.
The present perfect does not fit an imagined situation.

items.prompt: We would have helped you if you ___ us.

explanation.en: Third conditional: past perfect after if, because the result is would have helped.

optionNotes.en: The past simple belongs to the second conditional, not to would have.
Correct: if + past perfect, would have + participle.
Would never goes in the if clause.

items.prompt: If he ___ to bed earlier, he wouldn't be so tired at work.

explanation.en: The result wouldn't be shows an unreal present, so the if clause takes the past simple.

optionNotes.en: Correct: second conditional.
The present simple belongs to the first conditional, with will.
Would never goes in the if clause.

items.prompt: A: I can't decide whether to take the job. B: If I ___ you, I'd take it.

explanation.en: Advice uses the fixed phrase If I were you.

optionNotes.en: Correct: the fixed phrase for advice.
Would never goes in the if clause.
The present continuous makes no sense in this phrase.

items.prompt: If the bus hadn't been late, I ___ the beginning of the film.

explanation.en: The if clause has the past perfect, so the result needs would have + past participle.

optionNotes.en: Would + infinitive belongs to the second conditional.
Correct: third conditional result.
A result clause needs would, could or might.

items.prompt: She could have become a professional dancer if she ___ her knee.

explanation.en: Could have become imagines a different past, so the if clause takes the past perfect.

optionNotes.en: The past simple does not match could have become.
Correct: third conditional with could have.
Would never goes in the if clause.

items.prompt: What ___ if you found a wallet in the street?

explanation.en: Found in the if clause shows an imagined situation, so the question uses would.

optionNotes.en: Correct: second conditional question.
Will belongs to the first conditional, with a present tense after if.
Did you do asks about a real past event.

items.prompt: If the city ___ more cycle lanes, fewer people would drive.

explanation.en: The result uses would, so the if clause takes the past simple.

optionNotes.en: Correct: second conditional.
Would never goes in the if clause.
The present perfect does not fit an imagined situation.

explanation.en: The if clause has the past perfect, so the result needs would have + past participle.

optionNotes.en: Would + infinitive belongs to the second conditional.
Correct: third conditional result.
